tagline: A Mekong town facing the mountains of Laos — Phra That Phanom, an evening riverside walk, and an old Vietnamese quarter
introHtml: Nakhon Phanom sits on the Mekong, with the mountains of Laos rising on the far bank, which is why people come here specifically for the sunrise over the river. The town is easy to walk: there's a riverside road for catching the evening breeze, the Vietnamese memorial clock tower, and the old house where Uncle Ho Chi Minh once stayed. A little outside town you reach Phra That Phanom, one of the most revered Mekong-basin stupas for both Isan and Lao people. Around the province there are also birthday stupas spread across the districts to visit one by one. Nakhon Phanom works for the riverside crowd, the temple crowd, and the food crowd alike, with a clear Vietnamese influence running through the kitchen.
bestTime: November–February, when it's cool and pleasant for walking the riverfront and watching the sunrise. The Illuminated Boat Procession during the end of Buddhist Lent in October is the big annual event.

highlights.name: Phra That Phanom
highlights.blurb: A Mekong-basin stupa revered by Isan and Lao people alike. The white stupa with its golden top stands prominent in That Phanom district, with a steady stream of people coming to pay respects all year.

highlights.name: The riverside road and Laos mountain views
highlights.blurb: A walkway along the Mekong in the middle of town, looking across to the mountains of Laos. People come out to catch the breeze in the evening and to watch the sunrise over the water in the morning.

highlights.name: The Vietnamese quarter and Uncle Ho's house
highlights.blurb: Nakhon Phanom has long-standing Vietnamese community roots, with a Thai-Vietnamese Friendship Village and the house where Uncle Ho Chi Minh once stayed, reflected in both the architecture and the food around town.

highlights.name: The Vietnamese memorial clock tower
highlights.blurb: A clock tower in the town center built by the Vietnamese community, a landmark and photo spot of Nakhon Phanom that nearly everyone stops by.

highlights.name: Birthday-day stupas
highlights.blurb: Beyond Phra That Phanom, the province also has Phra That Renu, Phra That Tha Uthen, and Phra That Prasit spread across the districts, and people like to visit the stupa matched to their birth day.

highlights.name: The Illuminated Boat Procession
highlights.blurb: An end-of-Lent tradition on the Mekong where lantern-decked boats are floated down the middle of the river at night, a big annual event that draws people from across the region.

foodScene.name: Vietnamese food
foodScene.note: Naem nueang, mu yo, fresh spring rolls, and khao piak sen are found all over town thanks to the old Vietnamese community, and they're the most famous food in Nakhon Phanom.

foodScene.name: Isan food
foodScene.note: Som tam, larb, koi, grilled chicken, and bold bamboo-shoot soup are everyday meals for locals here just as across the region, available in every corner of town.

foodScene.name: Mekong river fish
foodScene.note: Riverside restaurants cook freshwater fish — grilled, in tom yam, as larb pla, and pla khang — to eat in the cool breeze with the Laos mountains across the water.

foodScene.name: Kuay chap yuan
foodScene.note: Soft Vietnamese-style flour rolls in a clear broth topped with white pepper and mu yo, a popular breakfast influenced by the riverside Vietnamese community.

foodScene.name: Riverside cafes
foodScene.note: Several cafes and coffee shops open onto Mekong views — sip a coffee while watching the sunrise in the morning or take a break before walking the riverside road.

foodScene.name: Mu kratha and grilled meats
foodScene.note: Mu kratha (Thai BBQ hotpot) spots are spread across town, a dinner that groups gather for, especially in the town center and near the riverside road.

foodScene.name: Mu yo and naem souvenirs
foodScene.note: Mu yo, naem, and Isan sausage are well-known take-home gifts, found at shops in town and the riverside market.

foodScene.name: Street food and the evening market
foodScene.note: The markets and riverside road in the evening have grilled and fried snacks and local sweets to graze on, along with river views and a cool breeze.

attractions.name: Phra That Phanom
attractions.blurb: A Mekong-basin stupa in That Phanom district, white with a golden top, revered by Isan and Lao people, with people coming to pay respects all year round.

attractions.name: Nakhon Phanom riverside road
attractions.blurb: A walkway along the Mekong in the middle of town, looking across to the mountains of Laos. People come out to catch the breeze in the evening and to watch the sunrise over the water in the morning.

attractions.name: Thai-Vietnamese Friendship Village
attractions.blurb: The Ban Na Chok village where Uncle Ho Chi Minh once stayed, with the old house and the story of Thai-Vietnamese ties on display, easy to walk through.

attractions.name: The Vietnamese memorial clock tower
attractions.blurb: A clock tower in the town center built by the Vietnamese community, a landmark of the town and a popular photo spot in Nakhon Phanom.

attractions.name: Phra That Renu Nakhon
attractions.blurb: The Monday stupa in Renu Nakhon district, where you can also see the way of life and the Phu Thai dance of the Renu community, a temple stop to pair with Phra That Phanom.

attractions.name: Phra That Tha Uthen
attractions.blurb: A riverside stupa in Tha Uthen district, similar in shape to Phra That Phanom but taller and slimmer, the Friday stupa that people stop to pay respects to along the riverside route.

attractions.name: Third Thai-Lao Friendship Bridge
attractions.blurb: A bridge across the Mekong linking Nakhon Phanom with the Lao town of Thakhek, a border crossing and a route onward to Vietnam through Laos.

attractions.name: Phaya Sri Sattanakharat plaza
attractions.blurb: A brass naga figure on the riverfront in the middle of town, a popular spot for offerings and photos, especially in the evening when people come out to walk along the river.
